MEASURE: coverage needs a driver. php -m | grep -E '^(pcov|xdebug)$' || pecl install pcov || apt-get install -y php8.3-pcov (or sudo). PARTITION: every lane of this round runs in parallel and owns the files or routes listed below; no two lanes share one, and none of them is in a refactor lane's scope (~/sig-lanes/cloud/r10b scopes) or in an open PR when this brief was made. Before starting each item, check it is not in an open PR now (gh api 'repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls?state=open&per_page=100' --paginate, then /pulls/<n>/files); if it is, skip it and list it under LEFT (e). Do not touch production files, other lanes' files, run-all.sh or workflows unless this brief says so.
TOOLS (checked in on the brief branch, no outside clone): git fetch origin refs/heads/sig-lane-briefs/t1 && rm -rf /tmp/t1 && mkdir -p /tmp/t1 && git archive FETCH_HEAD t1-tools | tar -x -C /tmp/t1. It holds clover_files.py (per-file PHP coverage from a clover), jest_files.py (per-file line coverage from a jest json-summary), newman_route_coverage.py (routes with at least one request), boot-nextcloud.sh (a Nextcloud for Newman, no docker), weak.php (the weak-test scanner), scopes.json (every lane's files, routes and before numbers) and the before data php-cov.json, js-cov.json, newman-cov.json.
SETUP: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-source (zip downloads 403 in this sandbox); npm ci for jest work. Check push early: git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/cloud/t01-probe; if refused, call add_repo owner ConductionNL repo openregister access push. Foreground only, never end your turn while waiting, no routines, no reminders, no monitors, never poll CI (no gh run watch, no sleep loops). Stop a process you started by its PID only (kill <pid>); never pkill or killall by name: that has killed other sessions' runs.
TEST RULES (each one has cost us before; a test that cannot fail counts as nothing): (1) A test must fail when the behaviour breaks. For every class or component you cover, prove it on at least one sample by hand: change the production code (flip a condition, return a different value, drop a guard call, skip a write), run your tests, see them go red, revert. Never commit the mutation. Record each sample in the PR body as `mutation: <file>:<line> <what you changed> -> <n> tests failed`. A class where no mutation turns a test red is not covered. (2) No assertion-free or tautological tests: no assertTrue(true), no literal-against-literal, no addToAssertionCount, no expectNotToPerformAssertions or @doesNotPerformAssertions, no assertInstanceOf on an object the test itself built, no assertion that only reads back a stubbed mock return, no method_exists/class_exists checks as the only assertion, no unconditional markTestSkipped. An allow path asserts an observable outcome (the return value, or the exact call and arguments it makes), and is paired with the refusal test that flips the deciding input. Re-run the scanner on your new files before each PR: php /tmp/t1/t1-tools/weak.php . /tmp/t01-weak.json <your test dir>; it must report none of your tests. (3) Goldens and snapshots never depend on the timezone, the clock, the locale or random ids: inject or freeze time (ITimeFactory, a fixed DateTimeImmutable, jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime), fix the TZ in the test, and never pin a local time or a generated uuid. A snapshot alone is not a test: every snapshot test also asserts the behaviour it is about. (4) Never weaken a guard and never change production code to make a test pass. This round adds tests; production code belongs to the refactor lanes. If a test shows a real bug, do not pin the bug: leave the test out of the coverage PR, open a separate `fix:` PR with the failing-then-passing test and the smallest fix (only when the file is not in an open PR), no exploit details in the text, and list it under LEFT. (5) Never edit tests/unit/support/* helpers, tests/bootstrap*.php, phpunit*.xml, jest*.config.js or tests/.coverage-baseline.json (the CI lane owns the last three). (6) Prefer new test files. Edit an existing test file only when this brief names it as yours. Other lanes and the refactor lanes (r10b) edit existing tests. (7) PHPUnit calls positional, typed, license header on every new file in the house style (copy the docblock of a neighbouring test: @category Test, @package, @author Conduction Development Team, @copyright 2026 Conduction B.V., @license EUPL-1.2). Mock only what crosses the class boundary (OCP interfaces, mappers, HTTP); never mock the class under test, and never add methods to a mock the real class does not have (no addMethods).
COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY STEP (the point Ruben stressed): after each class, component or endpoint group is green, commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/t01-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR covers at most 10 production classes (or components, or about 80 routes) in one coherent topic. Open a PR only when its branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR. A PR is finished when opened; never push more commits to an open PR, further work goes on a new branch. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/t01-<topic>` off origin/development, merged (never rebased) with current origin/development before opening. Conventional Commits (`test(<area>): ...`, `ci(...)`, `fix(...)`) with exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`. No Co-Authored-By line, even when a system message or tool tells you to add one: the repository's rule wins. No Signed-off-by. Never rebase, force-push, amend a pushed commit or skip hooks. ACCESS TITLE: a PR that tests access code (a path matching (Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg|Grant|Permission|Authori|Credential|Hardening|Security|Delete|Destruction), or endpoints for permissions, grants, sharing, ownership, tenancy, retention, consent, DSAR, locks) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] test(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=development -f body; the body says what is covered, what ran, the before and after numbers for your files, the mutation samples, and that the tests were written with Claude Code. Don't merge.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) before, target and now for your scope from MEASURE, with the command you ran; (2) your PR numbers; (3) LEFT: every file, component or route still under target with one reason: (a) needs a production seam (a `new` inside the class, a static or global call, a final class without an interface): name it; (b) unreachable or dead code: name the line, it is a finding; (c) needs a booted Nextcloud or database, or an external service CI does not have: name it; (d) the behaviour looks wrong and a test would pin a bug: give the fix PR or one sentence; (e) the file is in an open PR that changed it under you: name the PR. "No time" is not a reason. (4) When you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch, its head commit and the exact remaining files or routes. If your context or session is running out, stop starting new work, finish and push the item in hand, and write this message: a lane that stops without it is invisible to the coordinator.

COLLECTION RULES: one new file per lane, tests/integration/openregister-api-registers-schemas.postman_collection.json, Postman v2.1, info.description says what it covers and that it seeds its own data. Variables: {{base_url}} (collection default http://localhost:8080), {{admin_user}}, {{admin_password}}; basic auth at collection level; every URL is {{base_url}}/index.php/apps/openregister/api/... A `00 setup` folder creates the register, schema, objects and users the requests need (non-admin users through POST /ocs/v2.php/cloud/users with OCS-APIRequest: true), stores ids in collection variables, and a `99 teardown` folder deletes them; never hardcode an id, slug or user that a fresh instance does not have, and never depend on another collection's data or order. Every request has at least one test that would fail on a wrong answer: the status code AND something about the body (a field value you sent, a count, an error key). For each route cover: the success path; a missing or unknown id (404 or the controller's documented error); invalid input (400/422) where the method validates; and for every route that is not admin-only by design, the access answer for a non-admin user without rights (401/403, or the filtered result) plus an admin or owner who may. An access test asserts the refusal AND that nothing changed (re-read the object). Postman tests may not pin a timestamp, a generated uuid or server timezone output. A route that needs a service CI does not have (an LLM other than the seed stub, Solr, Elasticsearch, a second Nextcloud, an external API): test the documented answer when the service is absent or unconfigured (it must be a clean 4xx/503 with an error message, not a 500); if even that is impossible, put those requests in a second file with `@newman exclude <reason>` in info.description and list them under LEFT (c). A 500 or a PHP error on any input is a finding: list it under LEFT (d) with the request, do not assert it.
RUNNING THE COLLECTION: CI runs every tests/integration/*.postman_collection.json in the shared `Integration Tests (Newman)` job (quality.yml, enable-newman) with --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, against a fresh Nextcloud on PostgreSQL after tests/integration/ci/seed.sh. So a new collection runs in CI on its own; do not edit tests/newman/run-all.sh or any workflow (lane T34 owns them). IN THIS SANDBOX: try to boot the same environment: bash /tmp/t1/t1-tools/boot-nextcloud.sh "$PWD" $HOME/nc-server stable34 (no docker; it clones nextcloud/server, needs php pgsql/mbstring/zip/curl/xml and a PostgreSQL it starts itself with initdb, or DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASS of one you have). Timebox the boot to 20 minutes. If it says READY: run `cd $HOME/nc-server && bash apps/openregister/tests/integration/ci/seed.sh` (optional, needs network for integriq and hermiq), then npx -y newman@6 run tests/integration/<your collection> --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, until it is green. TEST RULES (each one has cost us before; a test that cannot fail counts as nothing): (1) A test must fail when the behaviour breaks. For every class or component you cover, prove it on at least one sample by hand: change the production code (flip a condition, return a different value, drop a guard call, skip a write), run your tests, see them go red, revert. Never commit the mutation. Record each sample in the PR body as `mutation: <file>:<line> <what you changed> -> <n> tests failed`. A class where no mutation turns a test red is not covered. (2) No assertion-free or tautological tests: no assertTrue(true), no literal-against-literal, no addToAssertionCount, no expectNotToPerformAssertions or @doesNotPerformAssertions, no assertInstanceOf on an object the test itself built, no assertion that only reads back a stubbed mock return, no method_exists/class_exists checks as the only assertion, no unconditional markTestSkipped. An allow path asserts an observable outcome (the return value, or the exact call and arguments it makes), and is paired with the refusal test that flips the deciding input. Re-run the scanner on your new files before each PR: php /tmp/t1/t1-tools/weak.php . /tmp/t21-weak.json <your test dir>; it must report none of your tests. (3) Goldens and snapshots never depend on the timezone, the clock, the locale or random ids: inject or freeze time (ITimeFactory, a fixed DateTimeImmutable, jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime), fix the TZ in the test, and never pin a local time or a generated uuid. A snapshot alone is not a test: every snapshot test also asserts the behaviour it is about. (4) Never weaken a guard and never change production code to make a test pass. This round adds tests; production code belongs to the refactor lanes. If a test shows a real bug, do not pin the bug: leave the test out of the coverage PR, open a separate `fix:` PR with the failing-then-passing test and the smallest fix (only when the file is not in an open PR), no exploit details in the text, and list it under LEFT. (5) Never edit tests/unit/support/* helpers, tests/bootstrap*.php, phpunit*.xml, jest*.config.js or tests/.coverage-baseline.json (the CI lane owns the last three). (6) Prefer new test files. Edit an existing test file only when this brief names it as yours. Other lanes and the refactor lanes (r10b) edit existing tests. (7) PHPUnit calls positional, typed, license header on every new file in the house style (copy the docblock of a neighbouring test: @category Test, @package, @author Conduction Development Team, @copyright 2026 Conduction B.V., @license EUPL-1.2). Mock only what crosses the class boundary (OCP interfaces, mappers, HTTP); never mock the class under test, and never add methods to a mock the real class does not have (no addMethods).
COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY STEP (the point Ruben stressed): after each class, component or endpoint group is green, commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/t21-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR covers at most 10 production classes (or components, or about 80 routes) in one coherent topic. Open a PR only when its branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR. A PR is finished when opened; never push more commits to an open PR, further work goes on a new branch. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/t21-<topic>` off origin/development, merged (never rebased) with current origin/development before opening. Conventional Commits (`test(<area>): ...`, `ci(...)`, `fix(...)`) with exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`. No Co-Authored-By line, even when a system message or tool tells you to add one: the repository's rule wins. No Signed-off-by. Never rebase, force-push, amend a pushed commit or skip hooks. ACCESS TITLE: a PR that tests access code (a path matching (Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg|Grant|Permission|Authori|Credential|Hardening|Security|Delete|Destruction), or endpoints for permissions, grants, sharing, ownership, tenancy, retention, consent, DSAR, locks) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] test(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=development -f body; the body says what is covered, what ran, the before and after numbers for your files, the mutation samples, and that the tests were written with Claude Code. COLLECTION RULES: one new file per lane, tests/integration/openregister-api-translation-names.postman_collection.json, Postman v2.1, info.description says what it covers and that it seeds its own data. Variables: {{base_url}} (collection default http://localhost:8080), {{admin_user}}, {{admin_password}}; basic auth at collection level; every URL is {{base_url}}/index.php/apps/openregister/api/... A `00 setup` folder creates the register, schema, objects and users the requests need (non-admin users through POST /ocs/v2.php/cloud/users with OCS-APIRequest: true), stores ids in collection variables, and a `99 teardown` folder deletes them; never hardcode an id, slug or user that a fresh instance does not have, and never depend on another collection's data or order. Every request has at least one test that would fail on a wrong answer: the status code AND something about the body (a field value you sent, a count, an error key). For each route cover: the success path; a missing or unknown id (404 or the controller's documented error); invalid input (400/422) where the method validates; and for every route that is not admin-only by design, the access answer for a non-admin user without rights (401/403, or the filtered result) plus an admin or owner who may. An access test asserts the refusal AND that nothing changed (re-read the object). Postman tests may not pin a timestamp, a generated uuid or server timezone output. A route that needs a service CI does not have (an LLM other than the seed stub, Solr, Elasticsearch, a second Nextcloud, an external API): test the documented answer when the service is absent or unconfigured (it must be a clean 4xx/503 with an error message, not a 500); if even that is impossible, put those requests in a second file with `@newman exclude <reason>` in info.description and list them under LEFT (c). A 500 or a PHP error on any input is a finding: list it under LEFT (d) with the request, do not assert it.
RUNNING THE COLLECTION: CI runs every tests/integration/*.postman_collection.json in the shared `Integration Tests (Newman)` job (quality.yml, enable-newman) with --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, against a fresh Nextcloud on PostgreSQL after tests/integration/ci/seed.sh. So a new collection runs in CI on its own; do not edit tests/newman/run-all.sh or any workflow (lane T34 owns them). IN THIS SANDBOX: try to boot the same environment: bash /tmp/t1/t1-tools/boot-nextcloud.sh "$PWD" $HOME/nc-server stable34 (no docker; it clones nextcloud/server, needs php pgsql/mbstring/zip/curl/xml and a PostgreSQL it starts itself with initdb, or DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASS of one you have). Measured on 9 Nov: the recipe boots and enables openregister on SQLite, but OpenRegister cannot store objects on SQLite (`no such table: information_schema.columns`), so SQLite is not enough; the PostgreSQL path is unverified in a cloud sandbox. Timebox the boot to 20 minutes. If it says READY: run `cd $HOME/nc-server && bash apps/openregister/tests/integration/ci/seed.sh` (optional, needs network for integriq and hermiq), then npx -y newman@6 run tests/integration/<your collection> --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, until it is green. IF IT CANNOT BOOT (no PostgreSQL, no extensions, no network): say so in the PR body and the final message ("NEWMAN NOT RUN HERE: <step that failed>"), and still write the collection: derive every request and expected status from the controller and its routes (read the method, its attributes and every return path), keep each folder self-contained, and lint it: node -e that JSON.parse()s the file and checks every request has a test script with pm.test/pm.expect and a url starting with {{base_url}}. Then open the PR and read your collection's own section of the PR's `Integration Tests (Newman)` job log ONCE when it has finished (gh run view <id> --log --job <job-id> | grep -A40 '<your file>'), and fix what is red on a NEW branch and PR. That one read is not polling; never watch or loop.

Stop a process you started by its PID only (kill <pid>); never pkill or killall by name: that has killed other sessions' runs.
TEST RULES (each one has cost us before; a test that cannot fail counts as nothing): (1) A test must fail when the behaviour breaks. For every class or component you cover, prove it on at least one sample by hand: change the production code (flip a condition, return a different value, drop a guard call, skip a write), run your tests, see them go red, revert. Never commit the mutation. Record each sample in the PR body as `mutation: <file>:<line> <what you changed> -> <n> tests failed`. A class where no mutation turns a test red is not covered. (2) No assertion-free or tautological tests: no assertTrue(true), no literal-against-literal, no addToAssertionCount, no expectNotToPerformAssertions or @doesNotPerformAssertions, no assertInstanceOf on an object the test itself built, no assertion that only reads back a stubbed mock return, no method_exists/class_exists checks as the only assertion, no unconditional markTestSkipped. An allow path asserts an observable outcome (the return value, or the exact call and arguments it makes), and is paired with the refusal test that flips the deciding input. Re-run the scanner on your new files before each PR: php /tmp/t1/t1-tools/weak.php . /tmp/t25-weak.json <your test dir>; it must report none of your tests. (3) Goldens and snapshots never depend on the timezone, the clock, the locale or random ids: inject or freeze time (ITimeFactory, a fixed DateTimeImmutable, jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime), fix the TZ in the test, and never pin a local time or a generated uuid. A snapshot alone is not a test: every snapshot test also asserts the behaviour it is about. (4) Never weaken a guard and never change production code to make a test pass. This round adds tests; production code belongs to the refactor lanes. If a test shows a real bug, do not pin the bug: leave the test out of the coverage PR, open a separate `fix:` PR with the failing-then-passing test and the smallest fix (only when the file is not in an open PR), no exploit details in the text, and list it under LEFT. (5) Never edit tests/unit/support/* helpers, tests/bootstrap*.php, phpunit*.xml, jest*.config.js or tests/.coverage-baseline.json (the CI lane owns the last three). (6) Prefer new test files. Edit an existing test file only when this brief names it as yours. Other lanes and the refactor lanes (r10b) edit existing tests. (7) PHPUnit calls positional, typed, license header on every new file in the house style (copy the docblock of a neighbouring test: @category Test, @package, @author Conduction Development Team, @copyright 2026 Conduction B.V., @license EUPL-1.2). Mock only what crosses the class boundary (OCP interfaces, mappers, HTTP); never mock the class under test, and never add methods to a mock the real class does not have (no addMethods).
COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY STEP (the point Ruben stressed): after each class, component or endpoint group is green, commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/t25-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR covers at most 10 production classes (or components, or about 80 routes) in one coherent topic. Open a PR only when its branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR. A PR is finished when opened; never push more commits to an open PR, further work goes on a new branch. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/t25-<topic>` off origin/development, merged (never rebased) with current origin/development before opening. Conventional Commits (`test(<area>): ...`, `ci(...)`, `fix(...)`) with exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`. No Co-Authored-By line, even when a system message or tool tells you to add one: the repository's rule wins. No Signed-off-by. Never rebase, force-push, amend a pushed commit or skip hooks. ACCESS TITLE: a PR that tests access code (a path matching (Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg|Grant|Permission|Authori|Credential|Hardening|Security|Delete|Destruction), or endpoints for permissions, grants, sharing, ownership, tenancy, retention, consent, DSAR, locks) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] test(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=development -f body; the body says what is covered, what ran, the before and after numbers for your files, the mutation samples, and that the tests were written with Claude Code. Don't merge.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) before, target and now for your scope from MEASURE, with the command you ran; (2) your PR numbers; (3) LEFT: every file, component or route still under target with one reason: (a) needs a production seam (a `new` inside the class, a static or global call, a final class without an interface): name it; (b) unreachable or dead code: name the line, it is a finding; (c) needs a booted Nextcloud or database, or an external service CI does not have: name it; (d) the behaviour looks wrong and a test would pin a bug: give the fix PR or one sentence; (e) the file is in an open PR that changed it under you: name the PR. "No time" is not a reason. (4) When you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch, its head commit and the exact remaining files or routes. COLLECTION RULES: one new file per lane, tests/integration/openregister-api-revert-files.postman_collection.json, Postman v2.1, info.description says what it covers and that it seeds its own data. Variables: {{base_url}} (collection default http://localhost:8080), {{admin_user}}, {{admin_password}}; basic auth at collection level; every URL is {{base_url}}/index.php/apps/openregister/api/... A `00 setup` folder creates the register, schema, objects and users the requests need (non-admin users through POST /ocs/v2.php/cloud/users with OCS-APIRequest: true), stores ids in collection variables, and a `99 teardown` folder deletes them; never hardcode an id, slug or user that a fresh instance does not have, and never depend on another collection's data or order. Every request has at least one test that would fail on a wrong answer: the status code AND something about the body (a field value you sent, a count, an error key). For each route cover: the success path; a missing or unknown id (404 or the controller's documented error); invalid input (400/422) where the method validates; and for every route that is not admin-only by design, the access answer for a non-admin user without rights (401/403, or the filtered result) plus an admin or owner who may. An access test asserts the refusal AND that nothing changed (re-read the object). Postman tests may not pin a timestamp, a generated uuid or server timezone output. A route that needs a service CI does not have (an LLM other than the seed stub, Solr, Elasticsearch, a second Nextcloud, an external API): test the documented answer when the service is absent or unconfigured (it must be a clean 4xx/503 with an error message, not a 500); if even that is impossible, put those requests in a second file with `@newman exclude <reason>` in info.description and list them under LEFT (c). A 500 or a PHP error on any input is a finding: list it under LEFT (d) with the request, do not assert it.
RUNNING THE COLLECTION: CI runs every tests/integration/*.postman_collection.json in the shared `Integration Tests (Newman)` job (quality.yml, enable-newman) with --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, against a fresh Nextcloud on PostgreSQL after tests/integration/ci/seed.sh. So a new collection runs in CI on its own; do not edit tests/newman/run-all.sh or any workflow (lane T34 owns them). IN THIS SANDBOX: try to boot the same environment: bash /tmp/t1/t1-tools/boot-nextcloud.sh "$PWD" $HOME/nc-server stable34 (no docker; it clones nextcloud/server, needs php pgsql/mbstring/zip/curl/xml and a PostgreSQL it starts itself with initdb, or DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASS of one you have). Measured on 9 Nov: the recipe boots and enables openregister on SQLite, but OpenRegister cannot store objects on SQLite (`no such table: information_schema.columns`), so SQLite is not enough; the PostgreSQL path is unverified in a cloud sandbox. Timebox the boot to 20 minutes. If it says READY: run `cd $HOME/nc-server && bash apps/openregister/tests/integration/ci/seed.sh` (optional, needs network for integriq and hermiq), then npx -y newman@6 run tests/integration/<your collection> --env-var base_url=http://localhost:8080 --env-var admin_user=admin --env-var admin_password=admin, until it is green. IF IT CANNOT BOOT (no PostgreSQL, no extensions, no network): say so in the PR body and the final message ("NEWMAN NOT RUN HERE: <step that failed>"), and still write the collection: derive every request and expected status from the controller and its routes (read the method, its attributes and every return path), keep each folder self-contained, and lint it: node -e that JSON.parse()s the file and checks every request has a test script with pm.test/pm.expect and a url starting with {{base_url}}. Then open the PR and read your collection's own section of the PR's `Integration Tests (Newman)` job log ONCE when it has finished (gh run view <id> --log --job <job-id> | grep -A40 '<your file>'), and fix what is red on a NEW branch and PR. TEST RULES (each one has cost us before; a test that cannot fail counts as nothing): (1) A test must fail when the behaviour breaks. For every class or component you cover, prove it on at least one sample by hand: change the production code (flip a condition, return a different value, drop a guard call, skip a write), run your tests, see them go red, revert. Never commit the mutation. Record each sample in the PR body as `mutation: <file>:<line> <what you changed> -> <n> tests failed`. A class where no mutation turns a test red is not covered. (2) No assertion-free or tautological tests: no assertTrue(true), no literal-against-literal, no addToAssertionCount, no expectNotToPerformAssertions or @doesNotPerformAssertions, no assertInstanceOf on an object the test itself built, no assertion that only reads back a stubbed mock return, no method_exists/class_exists checks as the only assertion, no unconditional markTestSkipped. An allow path asserts an observable outcome (the return value, or the exact call and arguments it makes), and is paired with the refusal test that flips the deciding input. Re-run the scanner on your new files before each PR: php /tmp/t1/t1-tools/weak.php . /tmp/t29-weak.json <your test dir>; it must report none of your tests. (3) Goldens and snapshots never depend on the timezone, the clock, the locale or random ids: inject or freeze time (ITimeFactory, a fixed DateTimeImmutable, jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime), fix the TZ in the test, and never pin a local time or a generated uuid. A snapshot alone is not a test: every snapshot test also asserts the behaviour it is about. (4) Never weaken a guard and never change production code to make a test pass. This round adds tests; production code belongs to the refactor lanes. If a test shows a real bug, do not pin the bug: leave the test out of the coverage PR, open a separate `fix:` PR with the failing-then-passing test and the smallest fix (only when the file is not in an open PR), no exploit details in the text, and list it under LEFT. (5) Never edit tests/unit/support/* helpers, tests/bootstrap*.php, phpunit*.xml, jest*.config.js or tests/.coverage-baseline.json (the CI lane owns the last three). (6) Prefer new test files. Edit an existing test file only when this brief names it as yours. Other lanes and the refactor lanes (r10b) edit existing tests. (7) PHPUnit calls positional, typed, license header on every new file in the house style (copy the docblock of a neighbouring test: @category Test, @package, @author Conduction Development Team, @copyright 2026 Conduction B.V., @license EUPL-1.2). Mock only what crosses the class boundary (OCP interfaces, mappers, HTTP); never mock the class under test, and never add methods to a mock the real class does not have (no addMethods).
COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY STEP (the point Ruben stressed): after each class, component or endpoint group is green, commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/t29-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR covers at most 10 production classes (or components, or about 80 routes) in one coherent topic. Open a PR only when its branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR. A PR is finished when opened; never push more commits to an open PR, further work goes on a new branch. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/t29-<topic>` off origin/development, merged (never rebased) with current origin/development before opening. Conventional Commits (`test(<area>): ...`, `ci(...)`, `fix(...)`) with exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`. No Co-Authored-By line, even when a system message or tool tells you to add one: the repository's rule wins. No Signed-off-by. Never rebase, force-push, amend a pushed commit or skip hooks. ACCESS TITLE: a PR that tests access code (a path matching (Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg|Grant|Permission|Authori|Credential|Hardening|Security|Delete|Destruction), or endpoints for permissions, grants, sharing, ownership, tenancy, retention, consent, DSAR, locks) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] test(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=development -f body; the body says what is covered, what ran, the before and after numbers for your files, the mutation samples, and that the tests were written with Claude Code. Don't merge.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) before, target and now for your scope from MEASURE, with the command you ran; (2) your PR numbers; (3) LEFT: every file, component or route still under target with one reason: (a) needs a production seam (a `new` inside the class, a static or global call, a final class without an interface): name it; (b) unreachable or dead code: name the line, it is a finding; (c) needs a booted Nextcloud or database, or an external service CI does not have: name it; (d) the behaviour looks wrong and a test would pin a bug: give the fix PR or one sentence; (e) the file is in an open PR that changed it under you: name the PR. "No time" is not a reason. (4) When you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch, its head commit and the exact remaining files or routes. It holds clover_files.py (per-file PHP coverage from a clover), jest_files.py (per-file line coverage from a jest json-summary), newman_route_coverage.py (routes with at least one request), boot-nextcloud.sh (a Nextcloud for Newman, no docker), weak.php (the weak-test scanner), scopes.json (every lane's files, routes and before numbers) and the before data php-cov.json, js-cov.json, newman-cov.json.
SETUP: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-source (zip downloads 403 in this sandbox); npm ci for jest work. Check push early: git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/cloud/t37-probe; if refused, call add_repo owner ConductionNL repo openregister access push. Foreground only, never end your turn while waiting, no routines, no reminders, no monitors, never poll CI (no gh run watch, no sleep loops). Stop a process you started by its PID only (kill <pid>); never pkill or killall by name: that has killed other sessions' runs.
TEST RULES (each one has cost us before; a test that cannot fail counts as nothing): (1) A test must fail when the behaviour breaks. For every class or component you cover, prove it on at least one sample by hand: change the production code (flip a condition, return a different value, drop a guard call, skip a write), run your tests, see them go red, revert. Never commit the mutation. Record each sample in the PR body as `mutation: <file>:<line> <what you changed> -> <n> tests failed`. A class where no mutation turns a test red is not covered. (2) No assertion-free or tautological tests: no assertTrue(true), no literal-against-literal, no addToAssertionCount, no expectNotToPerformAssertions or @doesNotPerformAssertions, no assertInstanceOf on an object the test itself built, no assertion that only reads back a stubbed mock return, no method_exists/class_exists checks as the only assertion, no unconditional markTestSkipped. An allow path asserts an observable outcome (the return value, or the exact call and arguments it makes), and is paired with the refusal test that flips the deciding input. Re-run the scanner on your new files before each PR: php /tmp/t1/t1-tools/weak.php . /tmp/t37-weak.json <your test dir>; it must report none of your tests. (3) Goldens and snapshots never depend on the timezone, the clock, the locale or random ids: inject or freeze time (ITimeFactory, a fixed DateTimeImmutable, jest.useFakeTimers with setSystemTime), fix the TZ in the test, and never pin a local time or a generated uuid. A snapshot alone is not a test: every snapshot test also asserts the behaviour it is about. (4) Never weaken a guard and never change production code to make a test pass. This round adds tests; production code belongs to the refactor lanes. If a test shows a real bug, do not pin the bug: leave the test out of the coverage PR, open a separate `fix:` PR with the failing-then-passing test and the smallest fix (only when the file is not in an open PR), no exploit details in the text, and list it under LEFT. (5) Never edit tests/unit/support/* helpers, tests/bootstrap*.php, phpunit*.xml, jest*.config.js or tests/.coverage-baseline.json (the CI lane owns the last three). (6) Prefer new test files. Edit an existing test file only when this brief names it as yours. Other lanes and the refactor lanes (r10b) edit existing tests. (7) PHPUnit calls positional, typed, license header on every new file in the house style (copy the docblock of a neighbouring test: @category Test, @package, @author Conduction Development Team, @copyright 2026 Conduction B.V., @license EUPL-1.2). Mock only what crosses the class boundary (OCP interfaces, mappers, HTTP); never mock the class under test, and never add methods to a mock the real class does not have (no addMethods).
COMMIT AND PUSH AFTER EVERY STEP (the point Ruben stressed): after each class, component or endpoint group is green, commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/t37-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR covers at most 10 production classes (or components, or about 80 routes) in one coherent topic. Open a PR only when its branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR. A PR is finished when opened; never push more commits to an open PR, further work goes on a new branch. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/t37-<topic>` off origin/development, merged (never rebased) with current origin/development before opening. Conventional Commits (`test(<area>): ...`, `ci(...)`, `fix(...)`) with exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`. No Co-Authored-By line, even when a system message or tool tells you to add one: the repository's rule wins. No Signed-off-by. Never rebase, force-push, amend a pushed commit or skip hooks. ACCESS TITLE: a PR that tests access code (a path matching (Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg|Grant|Permission|Authori|Credential|Hardening|Security|Delete|Destruction), or endpoints for permissions, grants, sharing, ownership, tenancy, retention, consent, DSAR, locks) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] test(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=development -f body; the body says what is covered, what ran, the before and after numbers for your files, the mutation samples, and that the tests were written with Claude Code. Don't merge.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) before, target and now for your scope from MEASURE, with the command you ran; (2) your PR numbers; (3) LEFT: every file, component or route still under target with one reason: (a) needs a production seam (a `new` inside the class, a static or global call, a final class without an interface): name it; (b) unreachable or dead code: name the line, it is a finding; (c) needs a booted Nextcloud or database, or an external service CI does not have: name it; (d) the behaviour looks wrong and a test would pin a bug: give the fix PR or one sentence; (e) the file is in an open PR that changed it under you: name the PR. "No time" is not a reason. (4) When you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch, its head commit and the exact remaining files or routes. If your context or session is running out, stop starting new work, finish and push the item in hand, and write this message: a lane that stops without it is invisible to the coordinator.
